Build a file upload zone in vanilla JS: a drop area (drag-over highlights it), file input fallback, a file list with name/size, image previews, and simulated upload progress bars with cancel. Restrict to images (or accept filter).

Requirements

  • Click-to-browse opens the file picker
  • Drag-over highlights the drop zone
  • Drop adds files to the list (no duplicates)
  • Image previews rendered via URL.createObjectURL
  • Each file shows name, size, and a progress bar
  • Simulated upload with progress + cancel
  • Invalid type shows an error toast

Concepts: dragenter/dragover/drop · URL.createObjectURL · progress simulation · file validation
lessons.why:
• Prevent default on dragover/drop or the browser navigates away. Track a drag counter to avoid flicker on child enter/leave.
  • Progress: setInterval advancing 0->100 per file, or a slow-approach curve (p += (100-p)*0.1). Cancel = clearInterval + mark file failed.

lessons.name: Drag & Drop Reorder / Kanban
lessons.desc: HTML5 DnD with live reordering — the interview favorite that catches everyone.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Drag & Drop Reorder / Kanban
lessons.what:
Build a drag-and-drop list (or single-column kanban) in vanilla JS: drag items to reorder them, with a live insertion indicator (ghost) showing where the item will land. Support dragstart/dragover/drop; the list re-renders from state after every drop.

Requirements

  • Drag an item to reorder it within the list
  • Live visual insertion point while dragging
  • Drop commits the new order (state updates)
  • Only the dragged item moves (not a copy)
  • Drag handle or full-row draggable
  • Keyboard alternative for reordering (bonus)
  • Works with mouse only (touch is bonus)

Concepts: dragstart/dragover/drop · dragenter index math · state-based re-render · visual feedback
lessons.why:
• On dragover, compute the target index from the list items' bounding boxes and show a ghost line before/after that item.
  • On drop: splice the dragged item out of state and back in at the ghost index, then re-render the list. The source item keeps class dragging during the drag.

lessons.name: Toast Notification System
lessons.desc: A queue + auto-dismiss + stacking — the tiny system that separates widget coders.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Toast Notification System
lessons.what:
Build a toast notification system in vanilla JS: a toast(message, type) API (success/info/error/warning), toasts stack in the top-right, auto-dismiss after 4s with a manual close button, and multiple toasts don't overlap. Cap the visible stack (e.g. max 5).

Requirements

  • toast(message, type) exposes the public API
  • Four types with distinct colors/icons
  • Auto-dismiss after 4s with countdown (bonus)
  • Manual close button
  • Toasts stack cleanly (top-right container)
  • Max 5 visible; oldest is removed beyond that
  • A11y: role="status"/"alert" for each toast

Concepts: event emitter / pub-sub · DOM creation · timers · container pattern
lessons.why:
• Create one container div on init (fixed, top-right). Each toast is a div appended with a class per type.
  • Auto-dismiss: setTimeout(remove, 4000). For max N, when length > 5 remove the first child. Close button removes + clears its timer.

lessons.name: Chips / Tags Input
lessons.desc: Enter to add, Backspace to remove, dedupe, and backspace-on-empty — micro-interaction mastery.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Chips / Tags Input
lessons.what:
Build a chips (tags) input in vanilla JS: type a tag, press Enter (or comma) to add it as a chip; chips have an × to remove; pressing Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip; duplicates are rejected with a shake/error. Provide a value getter for the chips.

Requirements

  • Enter or comma commits the typed value as a chip
  • Chips render with a remove (×) button
  • Backspace on empty input removes the last chip
  • Duplicate values rejected with an error flash
  • Leading/trailing whitespace trimmed
  • Input cleared after committing a chip
  • Chips accessible: getChips() returns the array

Concepts: keydown handling · deduplication · chip removal · input width auto-grow
lessons.why:
• Handle keydown on the input: Enter/comma -> commit; Backspace with value=="" -> remove last chip; Escape -> clear.
  • Auto-grow the input: set its width to scrollWidth (or a hidden span mirror) so the text never overflows the pill row.

lessons.name: Snake on Canvas
lessons.desc: Game loop, collision detection, and input buffering on <canvas> — a classic hard round.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Snake on Canvas
lessons.what:
Build Snake on a <canvas> with vanilla JS: a grid-based snake that moves on a fixed tick, grows when it eats food, wraps or dies on walls (your choice — call it out), dies on self-collision, and a score/restart. Arrow/WASD input with direction buffering so a fast turn isn't lost.

Requirements

  • Snake moves on a fixed interval (grid tick)
  • Arrow keys + WASD control direction
  • Direction can't reverse into itself
  • Input buffering: two rapid turns in one tick both register
  • Food spawns randomly on empty cells
  • Eating grows the snake and increments score
  • Self-collision ends the game; restart button
  • Rendered on canvas with clear frame loop

Concepts: game loop · linked-list / queue body model · input buffering · canvas rendering
lessons.why:
• Model the snake as a queue (head at front). Move = unshift(newHead), pop tail (unless growing). Body rendering = draw each cell rect.
  • Input buffer: push direction changes to an array; on each tick shift one and apply only if not the reverse of the current direction.

lessons.name: Minesweeper (flood fill)
lessons.desc: Flood-fill reveal, adjacency counting, and chording — the Google hard favorite.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Minesweeper (flood fill)
lessons.what:
Build Minesweeper in vanilla JS: a 9x9 board with 10 mines, first-click-safe, reveal cells with an adjacent-mine count, flood-fill open zero cells (BFS/DFS), right-click to flag, a win condition (all non-mine cells revealed) and a loss on mine click. Timer + reset.

Requirements

  • 9x9 grid, 10 mines placed randomly
  • First click never hits a mine (move it)
  • Revealing a 0 opens its whole region (flood fill)
  • Numbers show adjacent mine counts
  • Right-click flags/unflags a cell (counter shown)
  • Clicking a mine reveals all and ends the game
  • Win detected when every non-mine cell is revealed
  • Reset reshuffles and restarts

Concepts: flood fill (BFS) · adjacency counting · game state · right-click handling
lessons.why:
• Model as a 2D array of cell objects {mine, revealed, flagged, adj}. BFS stack: push neighbors of revealed 0-cells within bounds, skipping visited.
  • Place mines after the first click using a candidate list excluding the clicked cell + its neighbors. adjacency = count mines among the 8 neighbors.

lessons.name: 2048 Game
lessons.desc: Tile merging, sliding, and spawn logic — the ultimate grid state-machine round.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? 2048 Game
lessons.what:
Build the 2048 game in vanilla JS: a 4x4 grid, arrow keys slide all tiles in that direction, equal adjacent tiles merge (each tile merges once per move), a random 2/4 spawns after each valid move, score tracks merged values, and the game ends when no moves remain (or 2048 is reached).

Requirements

  • Arrow keys slide + merge all tiles
  • A tile merges at most once per move
  • Random 2 (90%) or 4 (10%) spawns after a valid move
  • No-move-on-this-direction leaves the board unchanged
  • Score increments by merged values
  • Win banner at 2048 (continue optional)
  • Game-over detection: board full and no merges possible
  • Animated slide/merge feel (CSS transitions)

Concepts: grid transformation · merge logic · spawn logic · valid-move detection
lessons.why:
• Slide-left algorithm: per row, compress (remove zeros), merge adjacent equals once, re-compress. Rotate the board 4 times to reuse it for all directions.
  • Valid move = any cell changed. Copy board before the attempt (JSON/structured clone) to compare. Possible move check: any empty cell OR any adjacent equal pair.

lessons.name: Drawing Board with Undo/Redo
lessons.desc: Pointer events, stroke recording, and undo/redo snapshots — real product UX.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Drawing Board with Undo/Redo
lessons.what:
Build a drawing board on canvas: draw freehand with the mouse or pen (pointer events), pick color and stroke width, undo/redo stroke-by-stroke, and clear. Snapshots are stored as stroke arrays (not pixel images) so undo is cheap and lossless.

Requirements

  • Freehand drawing via pointer events (down/move/up)
  • Color and stroke-width pickers apply live
  • Undo removes the last stroke; redo restores it
  • Clear wipes the board
  • Stroke model: [{points, color, width}]
  • High-DPI aware: canvas sized to devicePixelRatio
  • Touch support (pointer events unify mouse + touch)

Concepts: Pointer Events · stroke vectorization · undo/redo stacks · canvas DPI scaling
lessons.why:
• pointerdown starts a stroke, pointermove appends points, pointerup closes it and pushes to strokes[]. Redraw = clear + replay every stroke on each change.
  • Undo = strokes.pop() into redo stack; redo pushes back. Because strokes are data, redraw is deterministic.

lessons.name: Virtual Scrolling List
lessons.desc: Render 100,000 rows as ~10 DOM nodes — the performance round everyone flubs.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Virtual Scrolling List
lessons.what:
Build a virtual scrolling list in vanilla JS: render only the visible window of a large array (e.g. 100,000 rows) inside a fixed-height scroll container. On scroll, compute the visible range, render only those rows with absolute/translateY positioning, and keep a small buffer. Variable row heights optional (bonus).

Requirements

  • Fixed-height scroll container
  • Renders only visible rows + buffer (e.g. 5 each side)
  • Row positions via translateY, not top (no layout thrash)
  • Handles 100k+ rows without lag
  • Scroll position stable when jumping to a row
  • Click on a row fires a callback with the row index
  • Resize/row-height change re-measures

Concepts: virtualization · scroll events + rAF throttling · translateY positioning · window/range math
lessons.why:
• scrollTop / rowHeight = firstIndex; visible count = containerHeight / rowHeight; clamp. Render slice [first-buffer, last+buffer] into a spacer div of totalHeight.
  • Use a container div with height = total rows * rowHeight, and absolutely position each row with transform: translateY(index * rowHeight). Throttle scroll with requestAnimationFrame.

lessons.name: Sortable / Filterable Data Table
lessons.desc: Sorting, filtering, and row selection — the most common dashboard component.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Sortable / Filterable Data Table
lessons.what:
Build a data table in vanilla JS from a JSON dataset (name, email, role, status, join date): click a column header to sort asc/desc with an indicator, a search box filters across columns, a status filter chips, and selectable rows with a bulk actions bar. No framework.

Requirements

  • Renders rows from a JSON array
  • Column-header click toggles sort (asc/desc + indicator)
  • Search filters by any column (case-insensitive)
  • Status filter (chips or select)
  • Row selection with checkboxes + bulk delete
  • Empty state when filters match nothing
  • Sorting and filtering compose together

Concepts: sorting comparators · filter predicates · table rendering · state composition
lessons.why:
• Keep state = {sortKey, sortDir, query, status, selected:Set}. Derive rows = useMemo-equivalent: filter then sort then render — compute a fresh array each render.
  • Header click: same key toggles dir, new key sets asc. Icons: ▲/▼. Select all checkbox handles header toggling.

lessons.name: WebSocket Chat UI (vanilla)
lessons.desc: A WebSocket client, message list, and reconnect logic — real-time from the raw API.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? WebSocket Chat UI (vanilla)
lessons.what:
Build a chat UI in vanilla JS talking to a WebSocket endpoint: send messages, render incoming messages (own vs other with different alignment), show typing indicator and online status, auto-scroll to the latest, and reconnect with backoff on disconnect. Include a message input with Enter to send.

Requirements

  • Connects to a WebSocket (ws:// or a mock)
  • Send message via input + Enter/button
  • Renders own vs peer messages with alignment
  • Auto-scrolls to newest unless user scrolled up
  • Online/disconnected status indicator
  • Reconnect with exponential backoff
  • Typing indicator (bonus)
  • Handles connection error gracefully

Concepts: WebSocket API · reconnect backoff · message rendering · scroll anchoring
lessons.why:
• Socket events: onopen/onmessage/onclose/onerror. Track connection state in a status banner. Reconnect: schedule ws = new WebSocket(url) with increasing delay, reset on open.
  • Scroll anchoring: if user is near the bottom (scrollTop near max) auto-scroll after append; otherwise show a "new message" jump chip.

lessons.name: Mini Reactive DOM Framework
lessons.desc: Reactive state -> DOM updates — the tiny framework behind Vue/Solid, built by hand.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Mini Reactive DOM Framework
lessons.what:
Build a minimal reactive framework in vanilla JS: a reactive(state) proxy, watchEffect(fn) that re-runs when its tracked dependencies change, and a bind helper that maps state to DOM nodes (text and attributes). Counter + conditional-render examples prove it works.

Requirements

  • reactive(obj): Proxy tracks reads and writes
  • watchEffect(fn): runs immediately, re-runs on dependency change
  • Dependency tracking: only props read inside fn trigger it
  • bindText(el, state, path): keeps el.textContent in sync
  • bindAttr(el, attr, state, path): attribute binding
  • Multiple effects on one property all fire
  • Nested state objects are also reactive

Concepts: Proxy · dependency tracking · effect scheduling · WeakMap
lessons.why:
• Track: global activeEffect; Proxy get registers (target, key) -> activeEffect in a WeakMap>>. Trigger: Proxy set runs those effects.
  • watchEffect: set activeEffect = fn, run fn(), clear. Batch with a microtask queue (Promise.then) so multiple writes in one tick run effects once.

lessons.name: Virtual DOM Diff (vanilla)
lessons.desc: createElement, mount, and patch — build the React reconciliation core in vanilla.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Virtual DOM Diff (vanilla)
lessons.what:
Implement a minimal virtual DOM in vanilla JS: h(type, props, ...children) creates vnodes, mount(vnode, container) builds real DOM, and patch(oldVnode, newVnode, parent) diffs and updates in place. Props diff by key; children diff by index; text nodes optimized.

Requirements

  • h(): vnode = {type, props, children} (text as strings)
  • mount(): creates real nodes from vnodes
  • patch(): same type -> diff props + children
  • patch(): different type -> replace subtree
  • Prop diff: set/remove only changed attributes
  • Children diff by index with reuse
  • Event props (onclick) attach as listeners
  • Keys for list children (bonus)

Concepts: recursion · diffing · event delegation · object comparison
lessons.why:
• patch props: iterate new keys -> setAttribute / addEventListener (skip if equal to old), iterate old keys missing in new -> removeAttribute. Compare with Object.is to skip.
  • patch children: walk both arrays together, patch pairs, append extras, remove leftovers. Text: if both strings and different -> node.textContent = newText.

lessons.name: Spreadsheet Grid with Formulas
lessons.desc: A grid of cells, formula evaluation, and dependency recalculation — the wildcard round.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Spreadsheet Grid with Formulas
lessons.what:
Build a spreadsheet in vanilla JS: a 10x10 editable grid (A1, B1, ...), clicking a cell edits it inline, cells support raw values and formulas like =A1+B2, =SUM(A1:A5), =AVG(B1:B10). Evaluate formulas with dependency tracking so editing A1 recalculates every cell that references it (topological order).

Requirements

  • Renders an editable NxM grid with column/row labels
  • Inline cell editing (Enter commits, Escape cancels)
  • Values persist in a state object keyed by cell id
  • Formulas start with = and parse references + SUM/AVG
  • Cells referencing other cells recalculate on change
  • Circular reference detection (error state)
  • Display vs raw value: formula shows its result

Concepts: formula parsing · dependency graph · topological ordering · grid rendering
lessons.why:
• Parse references with a regex for ([A-J])(d+). Build a dependency graph cell -> dependents. On edit, recompute affected cells in topological order.
  • Eval safely: build the expression by substituting referenced cell values, then evaluate with new Function(...)? Safer: write a tiny recursive-descent evaluator handling + - * / and SUM/AVG over ranges.

lessons.name: File Explorer (Folder Tree)
lessons.desc: A recursive folder tree with expand/collapse, CRUD, and rename — recursion in the DOM.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? File Explorer (Folder Tree)
lessons.what:
Build a file explorer in vanilla JS from a nested {name, type: 'folder'|'file', children?} tree: render the hierarchy recursively, folders expand/collapse with an arrow, files select on click, and the toolbar supports new folder / new file / rename / delete on the selected node. Empty folders, deep nesting, and indentation guides.

Requirements

  • Renders the full tree recursively (folder > file nesting)
  • Folder arrow toggles expand/collapse; state persists
  • Click selects a node (highlight + toolbar enabled)
  • New folder / new file creates a child under the selected folder
  • Rename edits the node name inline (Enter/Escape)
  • Delete removes the node and its whole subtree
  • Folder name length/path-depth edge cases handled
  • Indentation guides render for each depth level

Concepts: recursive rendering · tree CRUD · immutable tree updates · event delegation
lessons.why:
• Model state as a single tree object; all operations return a new tree (map over children recursively). Render one recursive function renderNode(node, depth) and compose containers.
  • Delegation: one click listener reads data-id, resolves the node path, then rerenders. Paths: keep a path array (indices) in data-path so operations can rebuild the tree immutably.

lessons.name: Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
lessons.desc: Recursive comment threads with reply, delete, and vote — the infinite-nesting classic.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Nested Comments (Reddit-style)
lessons.what:
Build nested comments in vanilla JS: a top-level comment box, replies nest recursively to any depth, each comment has reply / upvote-downvote / delete (with a confirm). Reply opens an inline editor, and every comment shows an author, relative time, and score. A collapse toggle hides a comment and all of its children.

Requirements

  • Comments render as a recursive thread tree
  • Reply adds a child comment to any depth
  • Inline reply editor (textarea + post/cancel)
  • Upvote/downvote increments a score (one vote per comment)
  • Delete removes the comment and all descendants
  • Collapse toggle hides a comment and its subtree
  • Authors + relative timestamps rendered
  • No framework: pure DOM building + event delegation

Concepts: recursive rendering · tree state updates · event delegation · voting state
lessons.why:
• Comment node = {id, author, text, time, score, children[]}. renderThread(comment) returns the DOM for that subtree; rerender the whole thread on every mutation (data is small).
  • Reply: keep editingCommentId in state; the editor renders inline under that node. Deleting = filter node out recursively via map over children.

lessons.name: JSON Tree Viewer
lessons.desc: Render any JSON as a collapsible, color-coded tree — recursion over mixed data.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? JSON Tree Viewer
lessons.what:
Build a JSON tree viewer in vanilla JS: paste any JSON (or load a sample) and render it as an indented, collapsible tree — objects and arrays expand/collapse with a toggle, primitives are color-coded (string green, number blue, boolean purple, null gray), keys are clickable to copy the path, and a search box highlights + jumps to matching keys.

Requirements

  • Parses JSON input (error state for invalid)
  • Objects and arrays render with expand/collapse toggles
  • Type-based color coding for primitives
  • Keys copy their JSONPath on click (e.g. a.b[0].c)
  • Search highlights matching keys and jumps to first
  • Large inputs stay responsive (lazy render children)
  • Empty object/array shown inline as {} / []

Concepts: recursive rendering · mixed-type introspection · JSONPath · lazy expansion
lessons.why:
• One recursive renderValue(key, value, path) returns a node. If value is an object/array, it creates a togglable branch that lazily renders children only when expanded.
  • Path: build by concatenation (array adds [i], object adds .key). For search, precompute a flat index of key paths once, then highlight/scroll on match.

lessons.name: Cascading Checkbox Tree
lessons.desc: Parent-child checked-state propagation with indeterminate boxes — recursive state math.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Cascading Checkbox Tree
lessons.what:
Build a cascading checkbox tree in vanilla JS from a nested permissions list (e.g. Settings > Notifications > Email): checking a parent checks all descendants, unchecking clears all, a partially-checked parent renders an indeterminate box, and any manual child change recomputes ancestors. A footer shows the total selected / total count.

Requirements

  • Renders a nested checkbox list recursively
  • Checking a parent checks its entire subtree
  • Unchecking a parent unchecks its entire subtree
  • Parent with some checked children shows indeterminate state
  • Manual child toggle recomputes all ancestors
  • Leaf count + selected count shown in the footer
  • Checkbox + label click both toggle the node

Concepts: recursive state propagation · indeterminate state · derived state · tree traversal
lessons.why:
• Derive, don't store: a node's state is computed from its children — all checked, none, or mixed. Store only leaf 'checked' booleans (or a Set of checked ids) and compute everything else.
  • A checkbox indeterminate property: set el.indeterminate (not a CSS class). After any change, walk up recomputing each ancestor from its children.

lessons.name: Directory Size Calculator
lessons.desc: Recursive size aggregation over a fake filesystem — the math behind disk-usage tools.
lessons.q: Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Directory Size Calculator
lessons.what:
Build a directory size calculator in vanilla JS: a fake file tree where files carry byte sizes and folders aggregate their subtree total, rendered with each node's size right-aligned. Expand/collapse folders, sort children by size desc, and a 'calculate all' scan that animates folder totals filling in (walking the tree recursively with a delay).

Requirements

  • File tree with per-file sizes and folders aggregating subtrees
  • Size shown right-aligned per row, formatted (B/KB/MB)
  • Expand/collapse folders
  • Sort children by size descending (toggle)
  • Scan animation: folder totals fill in bottom-up
  • Recursive aggregation computes totals once and caches
  • Large trees: total displayed at the root

Concepts: recursive aggregation · post-order traversal · size formatting · animation timing
lessons.why:
• A folder's size = sum of children, computed post-order: size(node) = files sum + folders.map(size). Cache results in a Map so toggling sort doesn't recompute.
  • For the scan animation, flatten the post-order sequence into a list, then reveal each folder's total on a setTimeout/setInterval tick (or rAF).
